nodes.label: Amphail
nodes.rationale: Office of Lord Warder may rotate among the Amcathra, Ilzimmer and Roaringhorn families each Shieldmeet (fan source, unconfirmed).

nodes.label: Longsaddle
nodes.rationale: A Lords' Alliance member only because the Harpell wizards live there.

nodes.label: Lords' Alliance
nodes.rationale: Founded 1325 DR to oppose the merchant houses of Amn. Not a government: members rule themselves but set rivalries aside against shared threats. Turned inward in 1488 DR after Luruar collapsed.

nodes.label: Alagondar Bloodline Lock
nodes.source_file: Lore/The Lost Crown and Hidden Alagondar Vaults.md

nodes.label: Renaer's Council
nodes.rationale: The weaker faction in Neverwinter politics; some council seats are owned by noble houses.

nodes.label: Four Major Noble Houses of Neverwinter
nodes.rationale: Each has vassal houses. Three are bad (out for personal gain); one is good (stands with the people) and is currently weaker than the other three.
nodes.norm_label: four major noble houses of neverwinter

nodes.label: Powder-Crafting House
nodes.rationale: One of the largest houses, known for crafting and using the powder.

nodes.label: Neverwinter Mining House
nodes.rationale: The house that handles the mining.

nodes.label: The Powder
nodes.rationale: No single family controls the powder.

nodes.label: Group Opposing the Gods' Overreach
nodes.rationale: Thinks the gods are overstepping; uses Shar's tactics openly and blames her for what it does. Goals, progress and story direction still undecided.

nodes.label: Abundant Magic (campaign decision)
nodes.rationale: Modeled on Critical Role campaign 4 (Araman): magic runs through institutions and the noble houses are a threat you can't just fight. Heads of houses are level 10-15; there may be no magic shops as such.

nodes.label: Waterdeep: Dragon Heist (1492 DR)
nodes.rationale: In this world it went Manshoon's way (the winter branch). The party foiled Manshoon's scheme and recovered Dagult's hoard.

nodes.label: Manshoon's Simulacrum
nodes.rationale: Survived 1492 with an estimated 4 of 18 spell slots and can never regain them; Manshoon has not recast simulacrum since because that would destroy it.

nodes.label: Dagult's Hidden Hoard (500,000 gold dragons)
nodes.rationale: Returned to Waterdeep; per the book Laeral lets the party keep a 50,000 gp finder's fee.

nodes.label: Brandath Mausoleum
nodes.rationale: In the winter branch the vault is entered through it, and only Brandath blood passes its guardian, so Renaer went into the vault with the party.

nodes.label: Baldur's Gate Code of Law
nodes.rationale: Strict and complex; favours patriars, diplomats, the Fist and the Watch. Punishments fit the crime: whipping or finger removal for violence/theft, forced labour for broken contracts, the stocks for disturbing the peace.

nodes.label: Council of Guilds (Daggerford)
nodes.rationale: Created by Duke Conan's charter c. 1280 DR; meant to be anonymous like Waterdeep's Masked Lords, but the town is too small for secrets.

nodes.label: Compulsory Militia Service (Daggerford)
nodes.rationale: Every citizen fit to serve must do three days a month regardless of gender or race; exemptions for the young, old, pregnant and those raising young children.

nodes.label: The Rabbit Sentence (1376 DR)
nodes.rationale: The Harpells could not drive out two feuding Malarite sects, so they permanently turned the most dangerous members into rabbits.

nodes.label: Mirabar Mapmaking Ban
nodes.rationale: So that enemies, Luskan above all, can't get intelligence on the city.

nodes.label: Death Penalty for Attacking a Councillor (Mirabar)
nodes.rationale: Stops anyone from wrecking a candidate's election.
nodes.norm_label: death penalty for attacking a councillor (mirabar)

nodes.label: Mirabar Mining Houses
nodes.rationale: Once fought openly; the Harpers revealed this was a plot by Hellgate Keep, Zhentarim and Luskan agents, after which the houses united.

nodes.label: Sane Magical Prices (SMP)
nodes.rationale: Chosen as the base price list (2026-10-11) because it deliberately prices non-combat and intrigue items high, keeping mind reading, disguise and anti-divination rare and valuable in an intrigue campaign.

nodes.label: MrRhexx: What They Don't Tell You About Magic Items
nodes.norm_label: mrrhexx: what they don't tell you about magic items

nodes.label: Never For Sale List
nodes.rationale: Wish-granting, chaos, economy-breaking, too-powerful, stat-boosting, plot-device and cursed items come only as treasure or plot.

nodes.label: False Detection (Rhexx enchantment)
nodes.rationale: Costs only 300 gp yet hides the wearer from divination and scrying; the closest SMP item costs 20,000, so the price must be decided before players find it in a secrets-and-scrying campaign.

nodes.label: Amulet of Proof against Detection and Location
nodes.norm_label: amulet of proof against detection and location

nodes.label: Bag of Holding
nodes.rationale: Watch item: optional lower price (~2,000) so it doesn't eat a level's gold.

nodes.label: Boots of the Winterlands
nodes.rationale: Watch item: SMP's 10,000 is an outlier; cold resistance isn't worth more than a Bag of Holding.

nodes.label: Neverwinter Rare-Item Seller House Rule
nodes.rationale: For an intrigue campaign: common and uncommon items in shops across the city, rare and above only from specific sellers so each purchase is a hook.

nodes.label: Silverymoon Written Public Debate
nodes.rationale: When a policy debate ran too long, Alustriel had the arguments written down, copied and handed out free; citizens argued among themselves and submitted written opinions, which she combined with her own experience to shape final policy.

nodes.label: Dagult's Ouster as Open Lord (1489 DR)
nodes.rationale: Dagult was ousted as Open Lord in 1489 DR for spending Waterdeep's treasury on rebuilding Neverwinter.
nodes.norm_label: dagult's ouster as open lord (1489 dr)

nodes.label: Watchful Order of Magists and Protectors
nodes.norm_label: watchful order of magists and protectors

nodes.label: Good Faction (On the Back Foot)
nodes.rationale: If factions are even there is no adventure; the Good side starts losing, with incompetent or absent leadership, so the party matters.

nodes.label: Ugly Faction (Tipping Point)
nodes.rationale: The Ugly faction is the swing vote: the Good side is too uncomfortable to court it while the Bad side will ally with anyone, so the party brokers or blocks that deal.

nodes.label: Sleeping Dragon's Wake
nodes.rationale: On the radar because it is the official 5e adventure featuring Iniarv's Tower, a ready-made dungeon for the Two Black Brothers thread close enough to Neverwinter to fit the stay-near-the-city plan.

nodes.label: Dungeon #69-73 Mere of Dead Men Series
nodes.norm_label: dungeon #69-73 mere of dead men series

nodes.label: Year of the Drawn Line (1525 DR)
nodes.norm_label: year of the drawn line (1525 dr)

nodes.label: Discovery of the Powder (1498 DR)
nodes.rationale: It took until 1498 DR because of the clean-up of the city after the Cataclysm.

nodes.label: Meltharond's Skeleton (Lich Rider Illusion)
nodes.rationale: Flying with Meltharond's animated skeleton makes witnesses think a lich rides her, which keeps rival dragons from attacking.

nodes.label: Zundaerazylym (The Laughing Wyrm)
nodes.rationale: Steel dragons are the weakest dragon type, so her human disguise and security matter: exposure could get her assassinated.

nodes.label: The Soft Claws
nodes.rationale: They lure evil dragons to lair near orc warrens or horde routes so either outcome helps: the dragon kills orcs, or orcs kill the dragon and its 'unguarded hoard' lures the next one.

nodes.label: Longbite
nodes.rationale: For her dream to work she must eventually give Longbite to all dragons, ideally at once so none gains an edge.

nodes.label: Never Tokens
nodes.rationale: The Never Return power sends a token to a secret safe house so tokens never fall into enemy hands.
